summary: Bala Sahai Shastri worked in Indology. He held posts at Panjab University, attested as Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1947.

Baladora Indrajothi studied at Oriental Studies Society and the University of Kelaniya. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Vidyalankara Pirivena (2008–2015), University of Kelaniya (2016–2019), and Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2019–2021).

Balaganapathi Devarakonda is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi (1993–1995) and the University of Hyderabad (1997–2004). He became a professor at the University of Delhi in 2015.
Baliram Shukla is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he is attested as Head of the Department of Philosophy in 2001 and as a professor in 2026.
Balram Shukla is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Delhi around 2002–2009. He became a professor at the University of Delhi in 2004.

Balthasar Bickel is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Zurich (~1993–1997). He held a post at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011) and served on the editorial board at the University of Zurich (~2011).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987. He served as a professor at Peking University, where he was later attested as an emeritus professor in 2026.

Banikanta Kakati was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and became Dean of Arts at Gauhati University in 1948.

Bapu Deva Sastri was an Indology scholar who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She served at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where she is attested as an associate professor in 2000 and as a professor in 2026.

Barbara Ambros is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Columbia and Harvard. She held several teaching posts before becoming a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2015.

Barbara Catharina Jacoba Timmer was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at Leiden University (~1919–1925) and the University of Amsterdam (~1925–1930), working under Marcel Cohen, Barend Faddegon, and Jean Philippe Vogel.

Barbara Diane Miller was a Tibetologist who earned her B.A. at the University of Michigan (1948) and her Ph.D. at the University of Washington (1958). She taught at Beloit College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Barbara E. Ward was a scholar of Sinology who studied at Cambridge and the University of London. She taught at Cambridge and London, held visiting professorships at CUHK and Cornell, and headed the International Institute for Environment and Development (1973).

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Berlin, Oxford, and the University of Vienna.

Barbara Harriss-White, who studied at Newstead Wood School, works in Indology and related fields. She held posts at the University of East Anglia (1979–1990) and the University of Oxford, where she became Emeritus Professor of Development Studies.

Barbara Mittler is a Sinologist and historian who studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University. She held a post at Heidelberg University starting in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a Tibetologist and scholar of religious studies who completed her B.A. at Queen's University and her Ph.D. at SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf. She held a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist who studied at Barnard, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch. She served as a professor at Barnard College and Columbia University, and AAS president in 1990.

Barbora Sojková is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Charles University, the University of Oxford, and UCL. In 2025, she held postdoctoral researcher positions at both the University of Oxford and the University of Zurich.
